correctness.rationale: For n>=4 the object is a finite simple tree, the vertex processing order uniform, and m(T) the mean greedy maximal independent-set size. Reconstructed the first-arrival recurrence m(T)=1+n^{-1} sum_v sum_{C in T-N[v]}m(C), the exact path sequence alpha and second difference (-2)^(k+1)/(k+2)!, and the published KC split into nonnegative off-path changes and the on-path F_j(a,b) sum. The rectangle checkerboard argument applies to the strictly decreasing, strictly convex kernel w_k=2^(j+k+1)/(j+k+2)! and g_k=w_k-w_{k+1}, proving the positive decreasing eta_j and strictly positive alternating on-path sum for bare-path length at least two. If length one, an off-path neighbor of x contributes at least 1+alpha_b-alpha_(b+1)>0; all remaining contributions are nonnegative. Thus nu(T′)>nu(T) for every proper KC shift, yielding uniqueness by induction and KC reachability. A separate NetworkX exact rational traversal checked 292 oriented proper moves on the 45 unlabelled trees of orders four through eight, every time strict. The finite tests are diagnostic, not the all-order proof. Published 2024 KMM&S non-strict lemmas are explicitly used.

originality.rationale: The October 26 Resultary full theorem proves the IDENTICAL headline uniqueness statement by strictness of only the FIRST proper move from the path, plus non-strict KC monotonicity for later moves. It fully covers that headline, and this has been explicitly credited; it does NOT assert or entail strict nu growth across EVERY proper KC move, a stronger structural assertion included in the submitted full finding and proved with a new decreasing checkerboard-kernel lemma plus the adjacent-endpoint case. KMM&S 2024 establish nondecreasing nu only. Best-of-knowledge originality is confined to this globally strict structural lemma; rebranding the already-known path theorem alone would fail O.
